summary: Trojan loader in @sqlite-labs/nodesql pulls in sibling package on require
details: The package is published under an @sqlite-labs scope and named 'nodesql', but ships no SQL-related code. index.js is a verbatim copy of the feross/buffer module with a single injected top-level statement, `var ins = import('@sqlite-labs/createsql');`, which dynamically loads the sibling package @sqlite-labs/createsql whenever a consumer requires @sqlite-labs/nodesql. Package metadata reinforces the mismatch: an empty description, a README that references an unrelated package name (@sql-access/nods, bare-stream), and a repository (guilderguzman/sql-link) that does not correspond to the shipped contents. The sibling @sqlite-labs/createsql is not present in this tarball, so its code runs from whatever is currently published under that name at install/require time. The loader pattern combined with the name/contents mismatch matches the lure-plus-sibling-drop shape rather than a legitimate library dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
